pl452452.description: Skidros or Scidrus was an ancient Greek city located on the Tyrrhenian coast of Lucania between Pyxus (Buxentum) and Laüs.

pl452488.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl452488.description: The ancient city of Elea / Velia was said to have been founded by Phocaean Greeks in the sixth century B.C. and then became an ally of Rome in the third century B.C.

pl643029512.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl643029512.description: The multi-phase acropolis of Etruscan Volaterrae has numerous important phases, beginning in the Archaic period. The monumental site continued to develop and grow during the Hellenistic period. It was identified archaeologically only in the nineteenth century. In the twentieth century it was the subject of major investigations under M. Cristofani and, later, M. Bonamici.

pl34221419.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl34221419.description: An Etruscan settlement located in the Mugello valley.

pl952976544.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl952976544.description: A riverine port near the confluence of the Tiber and Paglia rivers.

pl292680658.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl292680658.description: The Pian di Civita was the ancient urban area of Tarquinia.

pl685301277.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl685301277.description: Vitozza is an ancient settlement located near the village of San Quirico. Its rock-cut habitations were in use by the Etruscans and Romans and again during the medieval period, continuing up to the eighteenth century. Over 200 caves (columbaria) have been cut in the local tufo bedrock.

pl582578935.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl582578935.description: An Etruscan necropolis at Tuscania in use from the seventh until the first century B.C.

pl441559175.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl441559175.description: An Etruscan necropolis dating to the seventh-fifth centuries B.C. The ancient settlement associated with the site may have been Palmule.

pl481818.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl481818.description: A city founded in 627 B.C. by colonists from Corinth and Kerkyra.

pl143520698.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl830662330.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl830662330.description: An Etruscan rock-cut necropolis of San Giovenale.

pl595928541.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl595928541.description: The Necropolis of San Giuseppe is located along a cut tufo road or via cava near Pitigliano.

pl69910488.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl69910488.description: The "Cave of the Fates" at Praeneste is a sanctuary at the base of the city's terraced sanctuary of Fortuna. It was said to contain wooden oracular tablets.

pl980724743.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl980724743.description: A site with votive activity from the Archaic period and a later Roman house in addition to the basalt-paved Roman road.

pl76301894.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl76301894.description: The so-called Minor Acropolis is located on the hill to the south of the Porta Maggiore. This area is surrounded by the urban enclosure wall and is terraced in polygonal masonry. Two platform temples of unknown assignation are to be found here.

pl47730716.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl47730716.description: The so-called Etruscan Pyramid of Bomarzo is a megalithic, rock-cut monument at Bomarzo. It likely dates to the late Archaic period.

pl294262131.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl294262131.description: An Etruscan necropolis located 5 km from Tolfa with tombs stretching from the Orientalizing period to the later Hellenistic.

pl5043153.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl5043153.description: A Doric temple dating to the sixth century B.C., located in the modern piazza Castello in Taranto, Italy. It was initially attributed to Poseidon, but may have been dedicated to a different deity.

pl584868520.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl584868520.description: An Etruscan necropolis in Chianti in use between the seventh and fifth centuries BC.

pl559227570.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl559227570.description: Settlement in western Albania containing signs of habitation from the 6th-4th centuries BCE. Tentatively identified as the site of Arnissa (Ptolemy), it is the find-spot of a bronze equestrian figurine.

pl117215971.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl117215971.description: The fortified site of Tricosto di Capalbiaccio is located in southern Tuscany, some 6 km inland from the ancient Latin colony of Cosa (Ansedonia). The archaeological site was initially identified by means of a field survey led by Stephen L. Dyson (1976-1980). Beginning in 2009 the site was again investigated. The site had a long occupational life, beginning as a minor Etruscan center (ca. seventh century BCE) and continuing in use through the Middle Ages (tenth century CE).

pl584523669.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl584523669.description: An archaic Etruscan tumulus located near Comeana, Italy.

pl675780058.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl675780058.description: The Necropolis of Selva Miccia, located along the road leading to Vulci, contains tombs of the seventh and sixth centuries B.C., corresponding in phase to the elite structure excavated at località Le Sparne.

pl486020305.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl486020305.description: The extraurban sanctuary of Minerva at Portonaccio is an important Etruscan cult center. The temple dates ca. 510 B.C. and was adorned with acroterial sculptures, notably the famous "Apollo of Veii".

pl708026976.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl708026976.description: Necropolis in Pontecagnano containing fifty burials from the Orientalizing Period (725-550 BCE) and an additional six burials from the Lucanian period (4th-3rd centuries BCE).

pl112932917.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl112932917.description: Monte Aguzzo di Formello (Rome), the site of a tumulus along the road leading for Veii to the Ager Faliscus.

pl389050484.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl389050484.description: A sanctuary with twin temples located at the Etruscan port. The Pyrgi sanctuary was initially excavated by Massimo Pallottino in 1957. The so-called Pyrgi Plaques were discovered here in 1964.

pl562679827.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl562679827.description: The Sasso Pinzuto necropolis is linked with the Etruscan culture and is located near Tuscania, Italy. The necropolis was in use from the middle of the seventh century BCE until the fifth century BCE. A new cult area was discovered at Sasso Pinzuto in 2024.

pl926170979.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl926170979.description: An important later Etruscan and Celtic settlement in the Po Plain with signs of occupation in the Late Bronze Age and then again between the fifth and second centuries BC.

pl107065917.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl107065917.description: An Etruscan settlement covering some 17 ha located near the modern village of Gonfienti (Prato).

pl277432401.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl277432401.description: A tomb near Sesto Fiorentino, that dates to the seventh century B.C.

pl780853072.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl780853072.description: An Archaic settlement in Lucania located near moderm Oliveto Lucano.

pl698136498.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl698136498.description: A seventh-century B.C. Etruscan tumulus is located near Pisa.

pl127042385.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl127042385.description: Rock-cut tombs located along the remains of a road dating as early as the sixth century B.C.

pl127042386.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl127042386.description: A seventh- and sixth-century B.C. Etruscan necropolis located in the territory of Heba.

pl403180.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl403180.description: A port on the island of Ilva (modern Elba), so named based on the resting place of the Argonauts, according to Strabo.

pl403183.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl403187.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl403189.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl403189.description: A lead and silver vein deposit in Italy's Apuane Alps region, mined most extensively in the 16th and 19th centuries of the modern era. Scholars have long accepted a history of exploitation here going back to the Etruscan period. Metallurgical analysis of artifacts from the late Villanovan settlement at Veii may indicate early iron extraction in this vicinity as well (Saviano 2006).

pl403194.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl403211.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl403212.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl403212.description: Populonia likely derives its name from the Etruscan god 'Fufluns' and was an important maritime and commercial center of Etruria located in the Colline Metallifere.

pl403225.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl403230.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl403230.description: The archaeological site of Lago dell’Accesa, in the locality known as "La Pesta", is situated near the lake of Lago dell'Accesa. The site was situated so as to exploit local mineral resources, and the archaeological remains provide extensive evidence for habitation from the ninth through sixth centuries B.C.

pl403239.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl403242.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl403244.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl403245.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl403248.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl403248.description: A city of Tyrrhenian Etruria that came under Roman control in 280 B.C.; the Latin colony of Cosa was established nearby in 273 B.C.

pl403256.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl403256.description: An isolated tumulus with grave goods ranging in date from the seventh to the fourth centuries B.C.

pl403258.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl403271.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl403280.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl403280.description: An ancient city of coastal Etruria, Telamon was eventually razed by L. Cornelius Sulla.

pl403281.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl403282.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl403291.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl403291.description: The Etruscan Vatluna resisted Rome's influence in the seventh century BCE, although the city may have been the source of Rome's adoption of the curule chair and the fasces.

pl403292.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl403292.description: A major Etruscan city of North Etruria.

pl403295.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl412987.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl412987.description: Acquarossa was an Etruscan settlement that was abandoned in the sixth century BC. The settlement occupied a steep-sided plateau and had an area of approximately 32 ha. Its ancient name is unknown.

pl413009.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl413012.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413012.description: Ameria, claimed by Cato the Elder (quoted by Pliny) as the oldest town in Umbria, was an important center that may have gained Roman municipal status as early as 338 B.C., following the Latin War.

pl413022.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413022.description: The Aquae Apollinares were thermal springs located between Careiae and Tarquinii, perhaps to be associated with the Bagni di Stigliano or Bagni di Vicarello.

pl413032.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413032.description: Arretium (the Etruscan Aritim) was one of the duodecim populi Etruriae and described by Livy as one of the "Capitae Etruriae". The Romans captured the city in 311 B.C. and it became a station on the via Cassia.

pl413035.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl413044.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413044.description: *Aurinia/Saturnia was a settlement in Etruria. Dionysius of Halicarnassus claimed it was founded by the Pelasgians. Saturnia received a Roman colony in 183 BC.

pl413048.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413048.description: Axia was an Etruscan center located to the west of Viterbo.

pl413052.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl413054.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413054.description: Blera was a significant Etruscan settlement in the vicinity of Tarquinii. It lay along the line of the Roman Via Clodia. It received Roman municipal status and was enrolled in the tribus Arnensis. The city flourished in the sixth and fifth centuries BCE.

pl413061.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl413062.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413062.description: An ancient urban center in Faliscan territory adjacent to Etruria, Capena was sacked by the Romans in 390 BC.

pl413063.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl413066.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl413067.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl413068.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl413071.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl413072.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl413077.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413077.description: Cetamura is an ancient hilltop settlement with occupation phases stretching from the Etruscans to the Romans to the Medieval period. The site is located near Gaiole, Radda and Castellina in Chianti, Italy.

pl413079.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413079.description: The site of Le Ciliegeta, near the source of the river Arno, served as a rich stips votiva. The site was discovered in 1836. The finds included over 600 bronzes, more than 1,000 pieces of aes rude, 2,000 weapons, and other artifacts.

pl413096.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413096.description: Clusium, the Etruscan Clevsin (modern Chiusi), was a major city of Etruria. Lars Porsena was a sixth century B.C. king of Clusium.

pl413103.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413103.description: Corchiano was the site of a wealthy settlement in the Ager Faliscus that was in proximity to the Via Amerina.

pl413104.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413104.description: The environs of Corciano were inhabited by Etruscans and, later, there is evidence for Roman villas. In 1812, a series of bronze panels from an Etruscan parade chariot was discovered at Castel San Mariano di Corciano.

pl413112.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413112.description: Cupra Maritima was a coastal city of Picenum (regio V) assigned to the tribus Velina.

pl413114.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413114.description: Cures (also Cures Sabini) was a Sabine city in the Tiber River valley along the Via Salaria. The Romans conquered Cures in 290 B.C. under M'. Curius Dentatus and granted it status as a municipium in the tribus Sergia.

pl413118.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413118.description: Doganella was an important Etruscan settlement of the Albegna valley, occupied between ca. 600 and 400 B.C. The city may have comprised as many as 240 ha.

pl413121.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413121.description: Eretum was a settlement of the Sabines and is involved in legendary accounts of early Rome.

pl413124.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413124.description: Faesulae (modern Fiesole) was an Etruscan foundation called Viesul, Viśl, or Vipsul. The city was conquered by Romans in 283 B.C. Sulla would settle Roman veterans there. Citizens of the town supported the conspiracy of Catiline.

pl413126.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413126.description: Falerii Veteres was the principal city of the Faliscans. It is located on a tuff outcropping at the point where several tributaries of the Treia join to flow into the Tiber. After rebelling against Rome in 241 B.C., Falerii suffered serious reversals of fortune.

pl413133.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413133.description: Fescennium is the ancient name of a Faliscan settlement located ca. 5 km south of Falerii Veteres. The site, which was inhabited from the second millennium to the third century BCE, is often also called by the modern Italian name Narce (derived from an associated peak).

pl413135.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413135.description: Firmum Picenum was founded as a Latin colony in 264 B.C. with 6,000 colonists. It received municipal status after 48 B.C.

pl413156.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413156.description: Ghiaccio Forte was an Etruscan settlement, most likely founded in the fourth century B.C., that was sacked by the Romans ca. 280 B.C.

pl413157.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413157.description: The port of the Etruscan city of Tarquinia.

pl413158.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl413163.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413163.description: An ancient city of Picenum that may have originated as a colony established by Etruscans from Adria in the Veneto region. An alternate narrative suggests the city may have originated as a late sixth-century B.C. colony founded by Aegina.

pl413164.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413164.description: A Roman colony that was established in the third or second century B.C., Heba lay near modern Magliano. Funerary evidence indicates previous Etruscan occupation at the site.

pl413172.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413172.description: The Etruscan settlement of *Hurta (the modern Orte) was close to the Vadimonis Lacus where the Romans fought, and won, two engagements against Etruscan armies.

pl413178.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413178.description: An Umbrian center founded in the seventh century B.C. that became an important Roman municipality along the Via Flaminia.

pl413179.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413179.description: Originally a settlement of the Praetuttii located at the confluence of the rivers Tordino and Vezzola (modern Teramo).

pl413186.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413186.description: Luni sul Mignone is a site with archaeological evidence for habitation in the later second millennium BC, continuing into the Italian Iron Age. Excavations conducted by the Swedish Institute in Rome (1960-1963) exposed three phases of settlement activity.

pl413188.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413188.description: Magliano Sabina is located in Lazio, some 50 km north of Rome and some 30 km west of Rieti.

pl413192.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413192.description: An ancient settlement located near the confluence of the rivers Albegna and Elsa.

pl413206.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413206.description: The tumulus of Montariolo originally measured some 4 meters in height and 50 meters in diameter. It included more than 350 tombs. It was used during several phases, stretching from the ninth to the fifth centuries BCE.

pl413208.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl413209.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl413212.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl413213.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl413214.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413214.description: Monti della Tolfa, a volcanic group of mountains in the Anti-Apennines in the northern part of Lazio in central Italy.

pl413216.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413216.description: An Etruscan elite complex of the seventh and sixth centuries B.C. located at Poggio Civitate, a hill adjacent to the medieval town of Murlo and about 25 km south of Siena.

pl413217.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413217.description: Musarna is an ancient Etruscan settlement discovered in 1849 just west of Viterbo, Italy. The École française de Rome has been conducting excavations at the site since 1983.

pl413224.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413224.description: Nepet had become a Roman town before 396 B.C. when Livy dubs it, along with Sutrium, as one of the "keys" to Etruria. It became a Roman colony in 383 B.C. and a municipium after the Social War.

pl413226.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl413228.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413228.description: Numana was a settlement of ancient Picenum located south of Ancona.

pl413231.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413231.description: An ancient Umbrian city that became allied with Rome in 308 B.C.

pl413233.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413233.description: [Orcla] or Norchia is an ancient Etruscan settlement located near Tarquinia and along the line of the Roman Via Clodia.

pl413248.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413248.description: A city of ancient Umbrian and Etruscan origin, Perusia aided Rome during the Second Punic War but was sieged and reduced by Octavian in the first century B.C. during campaigns against Lucius Antonius. It was rebuilt by Augustus and became Colonia Vibia Augusta Perusia quite late, in A.D. 251-3, under Trebonianus Gallus.

pl413252.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl413258.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl413259.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl413266.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413266.description: Poggio Buco was a pre-Roman site located in the valley of the Fiora River. Its archaeological remains include those of a circuit wall and a necropolis. The archaeological site is located ca. 9 km west of Pitigliano.

pl413267.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl413284.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl413285.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl413288.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413288.description: An Etruscan city captured by Rome in 294 B.C., Rusellae's >2 mile circuit of megalithic walls represent an important early instance of stone fortification walling in the Italian peninsula.

pl413297.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413297.description: An ancient settlement, architectural complex featuring polygonal masonry, and associated burials at modern S. Erasmo di Cesi dates to the archaic period and has evidence for activity through the third century BCE.

pl413299.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413299.description: An Etruscan settlement evidenced by its extensive, surviving necropolis, which now lies within the Parco Naturale Regionale Marturanum in the administrative territory of Barbarano Romano, Italy. Its modern name is transferred from a nearby medieval church.

pl413307.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413307.description: Sarteano is located between the Val d'Orcia and the Valdichiana. It is known in particular for its rich evidence of Etruscan funerary culture.

pl413318.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413318.description: Sorano was a Villanovan and, later, Etruscan settlement.

pl413326.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413326.description: One of three towns of the Paeligni which possessed municipal rights.

pl413342.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413342.description: Tiora Matiene was the site of an ancient oracle of the god Mars. The Barrington Atlas tentatively placed it at modern Teora, near Barete.

pl413344.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413344.description: Tolentinum was a town of Picenum that is listed as having municipal status in the Liber Coloniarum.

pl413352.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413352.description: Trevignano Romano, located on the shores of Lake Bracciano, lies some 47 km from Rome. Archaeological evidence for Etruscan occupation, in the form of tombs dating to the eighth - sixth centuries B.C., has been discovered to the north of the modern town. A medieval castle was built there under Innocent III ca. 1200.

pl413356.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413356.description: An ancient city that traced its legendary origins to Ascanius, son of Aeneas. The site became an important Etruscan mercantile center and eventually achieved Roman municipal status in 88 B.C.

pl413373.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413373.description: Volsinii Veteres was one of the most powerful and important cities of Etruria, as it was the location of the important federal sanctuary located at the Fanum Voltumnae.

pl413374.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413374.description: Around the modern Italian town of Verucchio (Emilia-Romagna), a number of ancient necropoleis provide evidence for iron-age civilization and craft at a presumed settlement on the site lasting into the Roman period.

pl413383.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl413393.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413393.description: Vulci (originally Velch or Velx in Etruscan) was an Etruscan city 80 km northwest of Rome. Vulci was one of the duodecim populi Etruriae.

pl416806.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl416806.description: A shrine of Voltumna that served as the chief religious center of Etruria. The Etruscan League (duodecim populi Etruriae) was said to meet annually at the shrine. Archaeological excavations of the site of Campo della Fiera have been posited as the definitive location of the Fanum Voltumnae.

pl422802.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl422802.description: A settlement along the Via Laurentina that has yielded significant evidence for protohistoric occupation, including funereal evidence of the eighth and seventh centuries B.C.

pl422803.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl422805.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl422805.description: A statio in Latium located at the intersection of the Via Latina and the Via Labicana, near the modern Valmontone.

pl422806.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl422806.description: The road station of Ad Decimum corresponds with the archaeological area of Castel di Decima where archaeological excavations in the 1970s identified the remains of a settlement covering some 11 hectares that dates to the eighth through sixth centuries BCE. Excavations revealed not only habitation evidence but also several hundred tombs.

pl422811.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl422821.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl422821.description: Aefula was an ancient settlement of Latium that had disappeared by the time of Pliny the Elder, although the cult of Bona Dea there continued to flourish.

pl422829.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl422829.description: An ancient settlement of Latium located in the territory of the Aequi.

pl422831.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl422831.description: Alsium served as a port for Caere, together with Fregenae. A Roman colony was established ca. 245 BCE. The Antonine Itinerary places it 18 Roman miles from Portus at the mouth of the Tiber.

pl422832.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl422832.description: A small site in Latium (?1.2 hectares) that may have been fortified as early as the eighth century BCE.

pl422833.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl422833.description: Anagnia was a Hernican town that sided with Rome against the Volscians and later became civitas sine suffragio. By Cicero's time it received the status of municipium.

pl422836.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl422836.description: Antemnae is an ancient Latin settlement located north of Rome near the point where the Anio and Tiber rivers intersect. Connected with Rome's early history, Antemnae was involved in episodes such as the 'Rape of the Sabine Women' and Romulus is said to have celebrated a triumph over the Antemnates in 752 BC.

pl422837.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl422837.description: Antium ranked as one of the most important and most powerful centers of Latium and was captured by Rome at the close of the Latin War in the fourth century B.C. Imperial Antium was well known for its number of coastal villas.

pl422843.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl422843.description: Ardea was an ancient settlement of the Rutuli in Latium.

pl422844.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl422844.description: Aricia was an ancient Latin settlement and a member of the Latin League.

pl422852.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl422852.description: A town of ancient Latium along the line of the Via Appia, Bovillae is traditionally considered to be a colony of Alba Longa and was one of the thirty cities of the Latin League.

pl422855.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl422855.description: Buon Riposo is a small, fortified settlement covering some 2 hectares. Its fortifications date to the seventh century BCE or later.

pl422857.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl422859.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl422859.description: Caere (also known as Cisra or Cerveteri) was a major Etruscan polis located ca. 50 km north-northwest of Rome in southern Etruria.

pl422862.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl422862.description: Campoverde (Lazio) lies some 60 km south of Rome. In 1977-1978 a quantity of votive material was recovered from a body of water known as the "Laghetto del Monsignore". This spring-fed body of water was interpreted as an open-air votive depository.

pl422876.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl422880.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl422884.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl422884.description: Castel Savello takes its name from a fifteenth-century fortress of the Savelli family at Albano Laziale. Funerary evidence associated with the Latial culture has been documented here.

pl422898.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl422898.description: Collatia was an ancient city of Latium located between Gabii and the Anio River. A colony of Alba Longa, Collatia was one of the most ancient cities of Latium. Subjugated by Rome under the Tarquins, Collatia would decline during the Republican period and numbers among the lost Latin cities by the accounting of Pliny the Elder.

pl422904.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl422904.description: Colle Rotondo was the site of a prehistoric settlement inhabited from the Bronze Age until the early Iron Age.

pl422909.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl422909.description: A Latin center in the Monti Lepini that was already a Roman municipium by 211 B.C.

pl422910.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl422910.description: An ancient town of Latium connected with the origins of Servius Tullius.

pl422914.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl422914.description: An ancient town of Latium located at the headwaters of the Allia River, very close to the territory of the Sabines, Crustumerium figures in Rome's early history. The Romans conquered the site in 500 B.C. and formed the tribus Crustumina or Clustumina in 471 B.C.

pl422916.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl422916.description: The Arval Brethren cultivated the cult of the Dea Dia. The remains of this Augustan era temple, located at La Tavernaccia restaurant in the Magliana Vecchia neighborhood of Rome, are subterranean and not open to the public.

pl422917.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl422917.description: A site sacred to Diana near Lake Nemi, comprised of a Tuscan-style sanctuary and a sacred grove.

pl422921.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl422921.description: An ancient city of Latium that was said to have been conquered by Ancus Marcius, Ficana was located near the eleventh mile of the Via Ostiensis. Excavation at the site has produced important evidence for the urban center beginning from the eighth century BC. Pliny the Elder mentions Ficana as one of the lost cities of Latium.

pl422922.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl422922.description: Ficulea was an ancient city of Latium situated between Rome and Nomentum.

pl422923.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl422923.description: Fidenae was an ancient city of Latium.

pl422932.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl422932.description: An ancient Latin city located on the line of the Republican Via Praenestina connecting Rome to Praeneste. Gabii is allied to Rome from an early date and flourished during the archaic period, declining by the time of Augustus.

pl422949.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl422949.description: An important Latial sanctuary of Iuppiter located on Mons Albanus (modern Monte Cavo).

pl422952.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl422952.description: Originally a member of the Latin League, the city of Labicum was taken by the Romans ca. 418 B.C. By the time of Augustus, the site was almost certainly deserted and its precise location remains debated today.

pl422956.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl422956.description: Lanuvium was an important city of Latium located south of the Alban Hills. After opposing Rome at the battles of Aricia (504 B.C.) and Lake Regillus (496 B.C.), Lanuvium was captured by the Romans in 338 B.C.

pl422960.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl422960.description: An ancient city of Latium on the Numicus River that was founded, according to Virgil, by Aeneas.

pl422976.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl422976.description: Monteroni, near Ladispoli, is the site of an Etruscan necropolis.

pl422977.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl422977.description: An Etruscan and Roman site lying 4 km to the west of Caere along the monumental road leading to Pyrgi. Until the early 1960s, the site was known for the monumental tumulus that Mengarelli had excavated in the 1920s. Subsequent excavation revealed other evidence, including an elite compound that served as a sanctuary.

pl422986.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl422986.description: The Latin town of Nomentum and Rome were linked by means of the Via Nomentana. In Livy's history the town, a member of the Latin League, is captured by Lucius Tarquinius Priscus. Nomentum was one of a number of towns captured by Tarquinius. The Romans granted the town civitas sine suffragio after 338 B.C.

pl422987.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl422987.description: Norba, located in the Monti Lepini, was a member of the Latin League (ca. 499 B.C.) and became a Latin colony ca. 492 B.C. The city was destroyed in the early first century B.C.

pl423002.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl423002.description: Piscina Torta is a place located in the Tyrrhenian coastal zone to the south of Ostia. The ancient place would have been part of the southern Tiber River delta. There would have been several natural ridges parallel to the coast and a coastal lagoon. The site has been connected with salt production since as early as the seventh century BCE and is linked with the city of Rome. The site has been the focus of several archaeological campaigns, applying techniques including surface survey and geophysical prospection.

pl423005.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl423010.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl423010.description: Ponte Mammolo is the modern name of an ancient bridge over the Aniene river. It gives its name to a neighborhood and metro station in the northeast part of the modern city of Rome. Archaeological evidence of ancient quarrying and a settlement have also been found in the vicinity of the bridge.

pl423013.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl423013.description: An ancient city of central Italy, the eighth and seventh century B.C. origins of which demonstrate high-level trade contact with the Eastern Mediterranean world. The city withdrew from the Latin League (499 B.C.) and opposed Rome in the Latin war; Cincinnatus eventually subdued Praeneste. Sulla founded a new colony there in the first century B.C.

pl423024.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl423024.description: The sanctuary of the god Robigus, located at the sixth mile of the Via Cassia. The Romans celebrated the festival of Robigalia on 25 April.

pl423026.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl423026.description: La Rustica was a Latin site located along the Via Collatina.

pl423034.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl423060.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl423060.description: An ancient settlement on the right bank of the river Astura, Satricum has a mixed heritage of Latins and Volscians. In 499 B.C. Satricum was a member of the Latin League, but was under Volscian control in 488 B.C. The site is noted for its sanctuary of Mater Matuta.

pl423081.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl423081.description: A Sabine town, 30 km east-north-east of Rome, Tibur was the seat of the Tiburtine Sibyl.

pl423099.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl423099.description: A Final Bronze Age settlement of four to five hectares in South Etruria.

pl423102.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl423102.description: An Iron Age settlement in Latium.

pl423108.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl423108.description: Tusculum was a Latin city of the Alban Hills in central Italy. After 381 B.C., Tusculum became the first "municipium cum suffragio".

pl423117.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl423117.description: Velitrae (modern Velletri) was an ancient Volscian settlement. In the Roman Republican period, Velitrae was attacked by Marcus Furius Camillus (379 B.C.) and again by Cincinnatus (377 B.C.); the Romans controlled the site by 365 B.C. The gens Octavia hailed from the city and a youthful Octavian spent time there.

pl245569735.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl245569735.description: The fortified acropolis of the ancient city of Arpinum.

pl99313926.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl99313926.description: A coastal Etruscan sanctuary that dates ca. 540-530 B.C. with additional architectural phases dating to the fourth through second centuries B.C.

pl289697636.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl289697636.description: An Etruscan necropolis located near the center of Sarteano with tombs dating from the sixth to the second centuries B.C. In 2003, the fourth-century painted tomb of the 'infernal quadriga' was discovered.

pl422997.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl422997.description: The Barrington Atlas Directory indicates that an ancient place called Pedum could correspond to the modern Corcolle in Lazio, Italy.

q212671.dateNote: Wikidata gives only the 7th century BC for his birth; 700 BC is only a placeholder. He died in 578 BC.

pl591465603.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl591465603.description: An Etruscan tumulus-type tomb at Asciano with artifactual evidence dating to the Orientalizing period.

pl720214763.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl720214763.description: A mid-seventh century BCE tumulus at Populonia with a diameter of 28 meters; part of the San Cerbone necropolis.

pl284018661.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl284018661.description: An Etruscan necropolis located on a tufaceous plateau overlooking the valley of the Fosso della Lenta. The tombs in the necropolis date between the seventh and fifth centuries BCE.

pl413321.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413321.description: Site of an ancient settlement that flourished between the seventh century BCE and the early sixth century CE, located west across the Tiber from the modern village of Attigliano in Italy. Piammiano is probably to be identified with "Statonia", which is mentioned in ancient sources.

q192998.dateNote: A semi-legendary king of Rome; his reign (578 to 535 BC) is traditional, and his birth year is not known.

pl851887955.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl851887955.description: An Etruscan settlement north of the Po river.

pl383603.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl383603.description: An ancient settlement. Modern Brescia in Italy.

pl383704.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl383704.description: Mantua (modern Mantova) is a city of Etruscan origin that received Roman citizenship in 49 B.C.

pl393374.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl393374.description: Altinum was the capital of the Veneti of northern Italy. The site was destroyed by Attila in 452 CE.

pl393379.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl393379.description: Ariminum (Rimini) is a Roman colony founded on the Adriatic coast in 268 BC.

pl393397.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl393397.description: An Umbrian and Etruscan city on the Savio River that passed into Roman control in the third century B.C.

pl393480.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl393480.description: A city of northern Adriatic Italy that served as the capital of the Western Roman Empire from A.D. 402 until 476.

pl662332234.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl426584.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl426584.description: A villa with beginnings in the early Republican period, continuing in use to the middle Imperial period.

pl426616.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl426616.description: A site to the west of modern Praeneste in Italy where surface material, remains of structures, and graves were discovered in the 19th century. These finds provide evidence for a settlement possibly dating to as early as the fifth or fourth century BCE but with likely occupation throughout the subsequent Roman period.

pl426638.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl432682.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl432739.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl432739.description: Cales was an ancient city of Campania of Ausonian origins. The Romans captured the town in 335 B.C. and established a colony there.

pl432745.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl432751.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl432751.description: Settlement on the island of Capreae.

pl432759.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl432760.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl432760.description: An ancient settlement along the Via Valeria, Carsioli was established as a Latin colony in the territory of the Aequi ca. 298 BC.

pl432778.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl432782.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl432782.description: Circeii received a Latin colony ca. 390 B.C. The remains on the site include an enclosure wall built in polygonal masonry. "Circeii 1" refers to the earlier Roman colony founded at the eastern side of Monte Circeo. The settlement eventually moved to the western side of the peninsula.

pl432794.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

This Latin city is said to have fallen to the Aequi and then been the subject of contention between the Aequi and the Romans, ultimately recaptured by the latter after Cincinnatus' victory at Mons Algidus in 458 B.C.

pl795348768.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl795348768.description: The remains of an ancient fortified center close to the town of Artena, Italy. The original settlement, of uncertain name, may have been established by the Volsci; both Ecetra and Fortinum have been suggested. The modern village was known as Monte Fortino until 1873.

pl109976883.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl109976883.description: A hilltop settlement with a long-term habitation, stretching from ca. 2000 BC to the first century BC. The archaeological site preserves the remains of 4+ mid-first millennium BC dwellings.

pl516051730.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl516051730.description: Field surveys, geophysical prospection, as well as targeted research and training excavations, have revealed the remains of a mid- to late- imperial rural settlement with evidence for agricultural activity. However, the earliest finds (e.g., bucchero) date to the sixth/fifth century B.C., indicating the likelihood of Etruscan settlement activities at this site. The entire site seems to have undergone severe recycling and reuse processes in late antiquity and the remaining structures have broken down systematically in modern times. Ongoing intensive agricultural activities affect the few archaeological structures that remain, resulting in a poor state of preservation.

pl403253.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl403253.description: A city situated on the Tyrrhenian seaboard and likely of Etruscan origin. Its early nature was that of a mercantile center. The city became a Roman colony in 89 B.C.

pl403257.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl413030.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413030.description: Arna was an ancient city of Umbria that was controlled by Etruscans in the fourth century BCE.

pl413036.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413036.description: Asculum (modern Ascoli Piceno) was the principal city of the Piceni.

pl413037.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413037.description: A Roman settlement built atop an earlier Umbrian one on a western foothill of the Apennines, Asisium received municipal status and was assigned to the Tribus Sergia. Totila destroyed most of the city in A.D. 545.

pl413045.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413045.description: Auximum (modern Osimo) is an ancient settlement of Picenum. The original foundation was likely carried out by Greeks from Ancona. The Romans made it a base for military operations from 174 B.C.

pl413058.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl413060.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413060.description: Camerinum was a town in Umbria on the frontiers of Picenum that was allied to Rome from 309 B.C.

pl413078.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413078.description: Chianciano Terme begins as an Etruscan site, with a temple located near the natural springs. By the first century B.C. the site was popular with Romans as a healing spa.

pl413097.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413097.description: A city of the Carricini Samnites. Its site was surveyed and partially excavated in the 19th and 20th centuries in the vicinity of modern Piano La Roma, a locality to the northwest of modern Casoli.

pl413098.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl413166.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl413171.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413171.description: Histonium, on the Adriatic coast, was a chief town of the Frentani.

pl413174.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413174.description: An Umbrian hilltown, Iguvium is best known as the find-spot of the Iguvine Tables.

pl413184.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413184.description: A sanctuary and grove of Feronia and an associated settlement located along the Via Tiberina in the territory of Capena.

pl413225.description: Nequinum/Narnia (modern Narni) was an ancient settlement in Umbria. It became a Latin colony in 299 BC.

pl413229.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413229.description: Nursia was the northernmost city of the Sabines.

pl413254.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413254.description: Pieve di Sant'Antonino a Socana, a Medieval parish church, is built atop the remains of an Etruscan sanctuary.

pl413256.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413256.description: Pisaurum (modern Pésaro) was founded as a Roman colony in the territory of the Picentes in 184 BC.
