pl442737.description: Praetorium Publilianum was the center of an imperial latifundium in the territory of Teanum Apulum.

pl442743.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl442759.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl442759.description: Sal(a)pia(i)/Salinae was an ancient city of Daunia.

pl50864837.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl50864837.description: A Roman villa located near Castel di Guido.

pl50864838.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl50864838.description: A Roman bridge over the Aniene river.

pl567970829.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl567970829.description: A Roman segmental arch bridge across the Bacchiglione river in Padua, Italy.

pl417977726.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl417977726.description: The Roman theater at Brixia was built during the Flavian period.

pl161590165.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl161590165.description: A villa site that includes a bathing complex, dating from the second to fourth centuries CE.

pl706597506.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl706597506.description: The so-called the Villa of Faonte was a Roman villa in Rome located between Via delle Vigne Nuove and Via Passo del Turchino. There are remains of a cistern (approx. 29.5 by 14 meters) now set in a garden area.

pl706597507.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl706597507.description: Remains of a villa built on several terraces.

pl917294321.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl917294321.description: Excavations have determined the location of the capitolium of Roman Verona, part of an extensive, terraced complex that underpins medieval and later structures of the city. The capitolium itself stretches from the northern end of the modern Piazza Erbe to the via Emilei, lying beneath the Palazzo Maffei, church of San Benedetto, Palazzo Malaspina and surrounding structures.

pl772313148.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl772313148.description: A large villa at Stabiae covering more than 17,000 square meters.

pl194091492.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl194091492.description: An archaeological site of the Roman period connected with the fluvial harbor of Rusellae.

pl544641873.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl544641873.description: A late Republican and early Imperial villa in the ager Cosanus noted for its turreted enclosure wall.

pl533417134.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl533417134.description: The remains of a Roman villa (first to fourth centuries CE) at Ladispoli. The surviving cryptoporticus gives the site its name.

pl819599643.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl819599643.description: A maritime villa of the first century A.D. adjacent to the port of Cosa.

pl248553771.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl248553771.description: The "Anfiteatro di Bleso" is a second century A.D. Roman amphitheater at Tibur (modern Tivoli in Italy).

pl879310882.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl879310882.description: A Roman milestone for the twentieth mile from Aguntum was found at modern Strassen in Austria.

pl166695363.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl166695363.description: A Late Roman villa and necropolis located at modern Imola in Italy.

pl612646272.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl612646272.description: The Cappella necropolis preserves a complex of underground tombs arranged along the ancient road connecting Misenum and Cumae. The earliest tombs date to the late first century BCE.

pl658246004.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl658246004.description: A theater constructed in Minturnae under Augustus or Tiberius, and further embellished under Hadrian.

pl674520031.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl674520031.description: The Roman baths of ancient Ferentium are located adjacent to the Roman theater.

pl500688552.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl500688552.description: Helvia Ricina flourished under Augustus and Tiberius and its theater is the largest in Picenum.

pl926867727.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl926867727.description: The Roman theater at Cales dates to the first century B.C.

pl285873044.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl285873044.description: A Roman bridge near Concordia Sagittaria.

pl65595829.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl65595829.description: The Villa Romana di Aiano-Torraccia di Chiusi, located near San Gimignano, is notable for a tri-apsidal courtyard.

pl616791790.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl616791790.description: The Roman theater at Caere (modern Cerveteri, Italy) is known especially for the sculptural program honoring Julio-Claudian emperors, including Tiberius and Claudius.

pl927235843.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl927235843.description: The hexagonal Trajanic harbor basin at Portus was built between 100 and 112. Its maximum diameter is approximately 716 meters.

pl423894082.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl423894082.description: Two coastal villas (villae maritimae) discovered in 2003 and 2004, respectively.

pl505987879.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl505987879.description: A villa rustica at Tortoreto, in the province of Teramo, with occupation beginning in the Late Republican period.

pl743823049.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl743823049.description: The remains of an extensive Roman villa have been documented (amongst other phases) in the village of Le Ferriere, on the grounds of the Casale del Giglio winery. This multi-period, multi-phase settlement demonstrates continuity of human activity, albeit with varying loci of focused activity.

pl69311541.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl617582458.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl617582458.description: Near Parentium (today Porec/Parenzo in Croatia), Cape Sorna (Zorna) first hosted a large villa maritima, and then a small early Christian church.

pl686909163.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl686909163.description: A Roman maritime villa located in Santa Severa on Italy's Tyrrhenian coast.

pl145326401.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl145326401.description: The so-called "Posto villa" at Francolise was located in the ancient Ager Falernus of Campania. Its remains lie 500 meters from the so-called "San Rocco" villa. This was a small villa rustica whose incipit comes ca. 100 BC.

pl965004100.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl965004100.description: A single-arch Roman bridge built during the principate of Augustus.

pl65232415.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl65232415.description: The remains of a Roman villa located adjacent to the Convent of San Giovanni del Palco in Taurano, Italy. The convent, founded in 1383 at the Niccolò Orsini, utilizes elements of the villa's structural remains in its foundations.

pl986457209.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl986457209.description: A coastal platform villa conneted with the Domitii Ahenobarbi.

pl270818822.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl270818822.description: A necropolis located on the southern outskirts of Rome. The necropolis is located near a villa site along a road running through the suburbium of Rome. Excavated between 1992 and 1993.

pl442773.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl442773.description: Canadian-led excavations between 1977 and 1984 uncovered a series of three Roman villas dating from the first to the sixth centuries AD at San Giovanni di Ruoti in southern Italy.

pl442777.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl442794.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl442794.description: An ancient settlement in the Abruzzo mentioned by Polybius in the account of the Battle of Geronium during the Second Punic War.

pl442802.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl443946.description: A Roman bridge over Torrente della Ginestra near Aequum Tuticum along the Via Traiana.

pl443954.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl443954.description: A much-repaired medieval bridge crossing the Aufidus (modern Ofanto) river. Long a traditional candidate location for the "Pons Aufidi" shown on the Peutinger map (thus BAtlas), recent survey work has found no evidence in the area consistent with a Roman-era bridge. The Pietra Dell'Oglio bridge (further south on the Ofanto) is of Roman date and now a more likely candidate. The Ponte S. Venere remains in use today for the Strada Statale 303.

pl443958.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl443958.description: An ancient Roman bridge over the River Ofanto, near Canusium on the Via Traiana.

pl446209.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl446209.description: Now unlocated, Acidios was a station on the Via Herculia according to the Antonine Itinerary, possibly located in the vicinity of Grumentum in the area of Marsico Nuovo.

pl710429514.description: A bridge along the Via Amerina, just south of ancient Nepet (modern Nepi in Italy)

pl960655569.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl960655569.description: A Roman bridge located near Narni, Italy.

pl538129499.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl538129499.description: A well-preserved Mithraeum with modern stone vault above ground and site below in Fertőrákos, Hungary, at the site of ancient Scarbantia.

pl861853679.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl861853679.description: A bridge on the Via Claudia Augusta crossing the Adige river near Maiensis Statio.

pl483627781.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl483627781.description: The so-called "Baths of Nero" are located near the Porta a Lucca in Pisa.

pl102529957.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl102529957.description: A Roman amphitheater dating to the first and second centuries.

pl714353568.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl714353568.description: Burial site near modern Pottenbrunn, Austria, containing 43 burials dated to the Roman period.

pl714351467.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl714351467.description: A Roman villa dating to the second century A.D.

pl322920273.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl322920273.description: A Roman villa dating ca. 50 B.C. located near Monte Gennaro.

pl652231746.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl652231746.description: A sacred precinct at the western end of Villa Hadriani, comprising two temples at opposite (north and south) ends of a plaza or garden, and (on the western edge of this complex) a small colonnaded hemicycle. Here, Hadrian may have planned to build a large, semi-circular temple-tomb for Antinous, in place of which his successors built the colonnaded hemicycle.

pl652231747.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl652231747.description: The so-called “Villa of Augustus” at Somma Vesuviana was first discovered in the late nineteenth century. The villa has been shown to have survived the 79 CE eruption of Mt. Vesuvius but was eventually destroyed by a volcanic event in 472.

pl990721366.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl990721366.description: A subterranean funerary chamber with three frescoes walls depicting animal and vegetal life, located around the third mile of the Via Appia.

pl698411340.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl698411340.description: Located outside the city wall, the Roman amphitheater at Carnuntum dates to the later second century. It could accommodate some 13,000 spectators. The amphitheater likely went out of use by the fourth century.

pl694724623.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl694724623.description: The precise date of the Roman theater at Lecce is uncertain, but it is generally assigned to the Augustan period.

pl379316151.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl379316151.description: The Aquincum Military Amphitheater dates to the reign of Antoninus Pius.

pl488345053.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl488345053.description: The Roman theater at Fiesole dates to the first century.

pl827074678.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl827074678.description: The Falerii Novi amphitheater is located north of the city walls.

pl923198883.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl923198883.description: A Roman bridge of the second century A.D. along the Via Traiana that crosses the torrente Buonalbergo.

pl226040114.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl226040114.description: The Roman amphitheater at Rusellae dates to the first century.

pl496511529.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl496511529.description: A Roman theater dating to the Augustan period.

pl121654605.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl121654605.description: The Aquincum Civil Amphitheater is the smaller of two Roman amphitheaters located in Budapest, Hungary. It was built between ca. A.D. 250 and 300.

pl230559832.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl230559832.description: The sanctuary and grove of Feronia located at the site of Lucus Feroniae.

pl594242500.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl594242500.description: The third of five shrines sacred to Mithras found near the site of Poetovio.

pl594242502.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl594242502.description: The Roman amphitheater at Sopron dates to the later first century A.D.

pl708445364.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl708445364.description: The Roman amphitheater at Luna was built in the second century, perhaps during the Antonine period.

pl442113997.description: Pausilipum was an ancient Graeco-Roman settlement on the Bay of Naples.

pl271130923.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl271130923.description: The Ponte sul Fosso di Biserano is a Roman aqueduct bridge of the Aqua Anio Vetus.

pl160277607.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl160277607.description: The remains of an unnamed Roman bridge at Fidenza are located in the public square known as "piazza Grandi". The bridge was part of the ancient Via Aemilia and carried the roadway across the Stirone stream. It likely dates to the first century CE.

pl634906148.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl634906148.description: The Catacomb of the Nunziatella or the Catacomb of the Annunziatella is an ancient catacomb located in Rome's Ardeatina neighborhood in the via di Grotta Perfetta. The catacomb was excavated on the site of a large Republican-period necropolis and does not seem to have been connected with any Christian martyrs.

pl480714925.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl480714925.description: A Roman villa located at the 1.6 km post of the via Tiberina, positioned on a tuff bank, today inside the Prima Porta cemetery.

pl361811831.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl361811831.description: The site of a Roman imperial-period villa in the modern Italian comune of Massaciuccoli Romana.

pl587781815.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl587781815.description: An arched Roman bridge across the Titerno near Cerreto Sannita in Campania.

pl267550313.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl267550313.description: The archaeological area of Cocciano located in the comune of Frascati, Italy, is the site of an imperial-period villa that is associated with Livia Drusilla and her son, the emperor Tiberius.

pl916222889.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl916222889.description: A Roman bridge across the Torrente Gran Caso located south of Ascoli Piceno.

pl239384580.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl239384580.description: The remains of a Roman villa on the Via Ostiense have been linked to Lucius Nonius Calpurnius Torquatus Asprenas.

pl791853467.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl791853467.description: The remains of a first-century BCE temple podium discovered at Sarsina have been identified as the Roman settlement's Capitolium.

pl710079070.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl710079070.description: A Roman maritime villa located at the southwest corner of the Istrian peninsula, about six kilometers south of Pola. According to Matijašić 1982, the remains of the villa are visible beneath the waters of Paltana Bay.

pl653874577.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl653874577.description: The Via Berneri columbarium was discovered in 2021 during utility work. This Roman tomb contained two sarcophagi, one of which carried a Latin inscription.

pl85250434.description: A necropolis at the thirteenth kilometer of the Via Aurelia excavated between 2007 and 2011. A total of 332 tombs were identified at the site.

pl275434516.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl169940092.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl169940092.description: A Roman villa with an associated bath complex destroyed by the AD 79 eruption of Vesuvius, the Masseria De Carolis site is located in the comune of Pollena Trocchia near Naples, Italy.

pl86666894.description: An amphitheater of the first century A.D.

pl467960423.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl467960423.description: The ruin called Ponte Taulella was once part of the Aqua Anio Vetus aqueduct.

pl356090423.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl356090423.description: A stone bridge at Genga, Italy, that is purportedly of Roman origin.

pl877349743.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl758766300.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl758766300.description: The Roman theater at Ocriculum dates to the early imperial period.

pl390040629.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl390040629.description: A temple dedicated to Octavian by a Lucius Calpurnius. It replaced a temple of ca. 194 B.C. that had in turn been restored by Sulla.

pl520736511.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl520736511.description: Imperial baths located on Fundi's decumanus maximus.

pl151530992.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl151530992.description: The Roman theater at Iuvanum is located at the foot of the acropolis.

pl395695982.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl395695982.description: The Roman amphitheater at Abella has been compared to the amphitheater of Pompeii.

pl95066748.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl95066748.description: The so-called Roman amphitheater at Egnatia/Gnathia dates to the Iulio-Claudian period. It is an elliptical structure with walls in opus Africanum that were revetted with painted plaster.

pl937974282.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl937974282.description: The Roman amphitheater at Rudiae is part of the complement of Roman buildings dating to the imperial period.

pl106009165.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl106009165.description: A Mithraic shrine of unusual size discovered at modern Marino, Italy in 1963.

pl316104222.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl316104222.description: The so-called "Portus Iulius" is an ancient Roman port complex on the Bay of Naples. Its remains are now submerged due to the bradyseism of the Phlegraean Fields. The archaeological remains were first rediscovered in 1956.

pl580782181.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl580782181.description: The site of a Roman villa that was discovered in 1904 in the Balácapuszta field of Vámos village in western Hungary.

pl83747513.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl83747513.description: The ruins of a Roman villa rustica were discovered in the 1990s along via Diego Fabbri. The site dates to the first century B.C. and remained in use at least until the fifth century A.D. The remains of a bath complex are substantial.

pl356540351.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl356540351.description: A Roman amphitheater located to the northwest of Nola and dating to the first century BCE.

pl710140373.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl710140373.description: Architectural remains consistent with a Roman-era villa maritima have been identified on both the north and south sides of a small bay at modern Valbandon in Croatia. Originally thought to represent a single establishment that wrapped the entire bay, more recent interpretations would see two separate architectural complexes.

pl524074853.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl524074853.description: A two-arched, stone-built footbridge across the Passer in Merano, South Tyrol.

pl798536747.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl798536747.description: The remains of the ancient port area of San Marco (Comune di Castellabate) date from the first century BCE.

pl991900272.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl991900272.description: The Villa dei Casoni is sometimes referred to as the Villa di Varrone, based on some scholarly assumptions that it once belonged to Marcus Terentius Varro. This late republican to early imperial platform villa is located near Poggio Mirteto, Montopoli di Sabina, Italy.

pl167811471.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl167811471.description: An uninscribed Roman milestone discovered in 1970 at Sillian, Tirol, Austria. The milestone corresponds to the 24th mile from Aguntum.

pl102937425.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl102937425.description: A Roman bridge along the Via Claudia Augusta.

pl415397391.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl415397391.description: A Roman bridge along the Via Salaria near Ascoli Piceno.

pl301156661.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl301156661.description: The so-called "Tempio di Venere" is likely part of a bathing complex dating to the reign of Hadrian. The surviving structure has an octagonal plan.

pl834043772.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl834043772.description: A Roman villa site near Rieti known initially from several cryptoporticus structures. More recent excavations have revealed a series of rooms, including some with mosaic pavement.

pl607885596.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl607885596.description: At Campetti - Decumano, in the southwestern part of Veii near the "Portonaccio" gate, there is evidence for a sacred complex that includes a therapeutic bath dating to the Roman period. Some residential functions emerged in Late Antiquity.

pl607885597.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl607885597.description: The site of a Roman villa complex covering ca. 10,000 square meters. The villa was built in the late republican period (second-first centuries B.C.) on the hillside adjacent to the Archaic Portonaccio sanctuary.

pl441255169.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl441255169.description: A Roman "Villa rustica" site dating to the second century.

pl371443773.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl371443773.description: An imperial Roman villa located near Potenza.

pl584868518.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl584868518.description: A large villa rustica inhabited from ca. 100 B.C. to A.D. 500, located near Montelupo Fiorentino in the mid-Arno Valley of northern Tuscany, approximately twenty km west of Florence.

pl536995786.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl536995786.description: The Roman amphitheater at Ancona could accommodate 8,000 to 10,000 spectators.

pl156209516.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl156209516.description: An aqueduct carrying water to Spello from the hills below Collepino.

pl471093749.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl471093749.description: A Roman bridge crossing the Carapelle stream in the territory of Ascoli Satriano.

pl296648276.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl296648276.description: An extensive maritime villa of the Roman period occupied the western and southern coasts of the Vižula peninsula, located near modern Medulin in Croatia.

pl93820013.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl93820013.description: Sometimes referred to as the "Anfiteatro Campano", the Roman amphitheater at Santa Maria Capua Vetere is the second largest in the Roman world. Begun under Augustus, it was further renovated under Hadrian and Antoninus Pius.

pl324666667.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl324666667.description: Crop marks, confirmed by a magnetometer survey reported in 2026, demonstrate the location and footprint of a monumental theater at the archaeological site of Fioccaglia di Fumeri.

pl136695106.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl271347289.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl271347289.description: The archaeological remains of the Roman amphitheater at Trebula Mutuesca are located at Monteleone Sabino in the Province of Rieti, Italy.

pl603582704.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl603582704.description: The remains of the so-called villa of Fralana belong to the villa rustica type. Mosaic floors have been discovered at the site, in addition to a productive area that may have included a Torcularium.

pl357565834.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl357565834.description: The so-called "Terme di Tito" is a terraced Roman villa site located in the modern comune of Castel Sant'Angelo near Lago Paterno.

pl547514740.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl547514740.description: Excavations at the archaeological site of Pietrarossa (Trebiae) revealed materials pertaining to a Roman domus in the territory of the ancient municipium. The site shows a long occupational history.

pl381242986.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl381242986.description: A seaside architectural complex of the Roman period in the Marechiaro locality of the greater metropolitan area of Naples, Italy.

pl747659417.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl747659417.description: A bridge of Roman origins located near Montesarchio.

pl329320003.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl329320003.description: A Roman bridge across the Basento river.

pl696470304.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl696470304.description: At Sant'Annèa are the remains of an extensive Roman villa located near the port of Gargano, about 3 km south of Lake Lesina. The villa probably originates in the late republican period and flourishes in the third and fourth centuries CE.

pl193750794.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl193750794.description: The Roman theater of Suasa was discovered in 2003 during excavations near the amphitheater. The semicircular structure measures ca. 55 meters in diameter and dates to the first century A.D.

pl786880550.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl786880550.description: A large seaside villa on two terraces overlooking the modern Santa Marina bay near Varbiga, Croatia. The villa lies on the northern coast of a headland; the major amphora workshop at Loron occupies the southern coastal site.

pl155158534.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl155158534.description: A Roman villa rustica belonging to the senatorial family of the Bruttii Praesentes that has been connected with Bruttia Crispina, the wife of Commodus. The villa was inhabited from the second century B.C. to the seventh century A.D. The villa's archaeological remains are found in the locality of Barricelle in the territory of the community of Marsicovetere in the province of Potenza.

pl113170099.description: The so-called "Ponte Fabio Massimo" or "Ponte del Diavolo" originally dates to the third century BC with subsequent reworking and reuse continuing to the Middle Ages.

pl442563575.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl442563575.description: The Roman amphitheater at Arretium was built during the late first and early second centuries. It measures 121 by 68 meters.

pl941089929.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl941089929.description: A Republican period cistern located along the present-day Via Polense in the Comune of Poli in Rome's eastern suburbs.

pl431558511.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl431558511.description: The archaeological remains of a villa near Licenza, Italy, that are traditionally connected with the Latin poet Horace.

pl125510816.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl125510816.description: A Roman villa and bath complex located in the valley of the Noncello River. The villa complex, whose original construction dates to the first century BCE, was likely rebuilt during the second century CE.

pl497311598.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl497311598.description: A large, rectangular cistern (Castellum aquarum) located near Poggio Murella was built in opus reticulatum.

pl823844102.description: A Roman-period bridge along the via Praenestina built of lapis Gabinus.

pl724216016.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl724216016.description: A Late Republican villa in Abruzzo that later became a productive estate. The archaeological remains of the villa are located in the locality of Piano S. Maria Arabona in Manoppello, Italy.

pl32694358.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl32694358.description: The so-called "Sacellum of the Augustales" at Misenum is an architectural complex located near the theater that was first built during the Iulio-Claudian period and dedicated to the Imperial cult. The complex was renovated during the second century, at which time one Cassia Victoria re-dedicated the shrine in honor of her husband, L. Laecanius Primitivus, who was a priest of the Augustales during the reign of Marcus Aurelius.

pl659743014.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl659743014.description: A villa rustica in Rome's suburbium with evidence for domestic production in the form of vats made from peperino tuff.

pl981864003.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl981864003.description: The remains of a Roman "Villa rustica" located adjacent to the Sanctuary of the Madonna di Canneto.

pl23219358.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl23219358.description: The Roman theater at Amiternum could seat approximately 2,000 people. It was abandoned after the fourth century and became a necropolis.

pl394869.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl394869.description: The remains of a Roman bridge that once crossed the river known as Uso are located at San Vito, Italy, in the environs of Rimini.

pl394872.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl394872.description: Excavated remains of a Roman bridge located on the modern Via Ponte Romano about 2km southest of Ceggia (Veneto), Italy. Aerial/satellite photographs often show crop marking corresponding to the associated Roman road and now-diverted watercourse spanned by the bridge.

pl403208.description: Fossae Papirianae refers to a navigable coastal canal and road station location along the Via Aemilia Scauri between Luna and Pisae.

pl403266.description: A Roman villa that was likely in use from the first century BC until the third century AD.

pl403927.description: A first century A.D. Roman aqueduct that carried water from the locality known as "Caldaccoli" to baths in Pisa.

pl409240.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl409240.description: Now unlocated, Turrita was a station (statio) near Pisae.

pl412992.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl412997.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl412997.description: A Roman road station, mentioned in the Antonine Itinerary. It was probably located somewhere near modern Valiano in the Italian province of Sienna.

pl413001.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413001.description: Aequiculi was a municipium in the territory of the Aequi.

pl413008.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413008.description: An ancient place, mentioned in the maritime portion of the Antonine Itineraries as between Centum Cellae (modern Civitavecchia) and Rapinium (modern Bagni Sant'Agostino). BAtlas identifies Algae with modern Torre Valdaliga; whereas NP considers it unlocated.

pl413011.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413011.description: Occupation of the Roman villa at Alviano Scalo begins in the first century BCE and continues until the fourth century CE.

pl413015.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl413016.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413016.description: Anneianum was located in the Etruscan Apennines, along the road from Faventia to Florentia.

pl413023.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl413024.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413024.description: Roman city situated on mineral springs known today as Terme di Cotilia or Terme di Vespasiano in the Sabina region, Italy.

pl413025.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413025.description: Located in Etruria, Aquae Passeris was frequented in antiquity for its thermal springs, as noted by Martial. The site is included on the Tabula Peutingeriana, placing it on the road from Rome to Volsinii. Its location likely corresponds to that of Bacucco, a comune to the north of Viterbo.

pl413042.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl413050.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413050.description: Baccanae was a road station along the Via Cassia.

pl413051.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413051.description: Badies is a site (vicus) along the Via Salaria mentioned in the Antonine Itinerary. Its location is no longer certain.

pl413076.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413076.description: Centum Cellae (modern Civitavecchia) was an ancient coastal settlement in Tyrrhenian Etruria. The emperor Trajan rebuilt the harbor at the site in 106/7 and Pliny the Younger mentions its name, Centum Cellae. Saracens destroyed the city in A.D. 812.

pl413090.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413090.description: A city of the Aequiculi located in the valley of the Salto river.

pl413093.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413093.description: Cluana was an ancient settlement in Picenum.

pl413099.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413099.description: A hilltop villa near Tifernum Tiberinum commonly associated with one of the villas of Pliny the Younger.

pl413100.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl413134.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl413138.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413138.description: Florentia (modern Florence / Firenze) was founded as a colony for military veterans ca. 80 B.C. by Lucius Cornelius Sulla.

pl413141.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl413142.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413142.description: Foruli was a Sabine town located between Amiternum and Interocrea.

pl413148.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413148.description: Forum Novum was a Roman town and an early medieval bishopric. It is located in the Sabine hills and was likely founded as a market center during the Republican period. It had achieved the status of municipium by the first century A.D. The market center seems to have remained active until at least the fourth century and by the fifth century, a bishopric is established there.

pl413152.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413152.description: A vicus of the Vestini located in the upper Aterno valley in Abruzzo. The ancient settlement was located some 15 km south of modern L'Aquila, in the vicinity of S. Maria di Forfona near Barisciano. Furfo lay on the Via Claudia Nova between Amiternum and Peltuinum.

pl413154.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl413160.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413160.description: Grotte di Torri is located on the left bank of the Tiber river in the modern comune of Montopoli di Sabina. It has been inhabited since pre-Roman times.

pl413180.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413180.description: Intercisa/Petra Pertusa was a road station on the Via Flaminia. The toponym derives from the rock-cut tunnel or galleria that dates to the reign of Vespasian.

pl413181.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl413181.description: A Sabine town that was later known as a mansio on the course of the Via Salaria.

pl413182.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

The site is mentioned in the Liber Pontificalis as that of a large imperial villa in which Helena, mother of Constantine I, lived. Archaeological work conducted in the late 1990s identified the remains of substantial Republican-period villas in the same area, with evidence of both elite dwellings and viticulture. The villas identified are the Villa della Piscina and the Villa Ad Duas Lauros.

pl104638958.description: An ancient place at modern Cantiano may have stood along the line of a branch of the Via Flaminia. The so-called "Sassoferrato milestone" was located about one mile from Cantiano (CIL 6629).

pl104638959.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl104638959.description: Bibbiena likely originated as an Etruscan hilltop settlement. A Medieval castle is eventually built atop the hill, which stands 425 metres (1,394 ft) above sea level.

pl362684055.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl362684055.description: A villa of the second century AD that was destroyed by a flood in the fourth century.

pl56738064.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl56738064.description: An Etruscan sanctuary located on Monte Landro northwest of Lake Bolsena.

pl144825573.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl144825573.description: An important villa that was excavated during the construction of the University of Rome 'Tor Vergata' in the 1970s, now reinterred. The Carcaricola villa begins in the middle of the second century B.C. and continues in use until the second century A.D.

pl305770200.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl305770200.description: A series of noncontinuous fortifications are extant on Mount Gildone (elevation 902 meters) that enclose part of an upland plateau. A nucleus of 23 Samnite tombs was also discovered in the vicinity.

pl579570263.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl579570263.description: A series of villa rustica located along the road to Cambodunum.

pl736595947.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl736595947.description: A planned Etruscan settlement in the Albegna valley along the line of the Via Aurelia founded, perhaps, ca. 570 B.C. The site offers evidence for iron working.

pl555723846.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl555723846.description: The modern Acquapendente was settled in pre-Roman times but is known historically from the Middle Ages onward.

pl118164239.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl118164239.description: A farm site with a least two occupation phases - one dating between the second century BC and early first century AD and the second between the fourth and fifth centuries AD.

pl648012835.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl648012835.description: Remains of polygonal masonry fortification are extant at Olevano Romano in Italy, which is presumed to be the site of a fortified oppidum of the Aequi. The modern comune of Olevano Romano is located in Lazio, about 45 km to the east of Rome. Pre-Roman polygonal masonry walls underlie medieval architecture in the centro storico.

pl298394661.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl298394661.description: An oppidum located on Michelsberg hill in Bavaria, occupied from ca. 500 BC until the first century BC.

pl20585718.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl20585718.description: The modern Vasanello lies on the line of the Via Amerina. Some scholars have long speculated that it is a candidate for being the ancient "Castellum Amerinum". Settlement at the site begins with the Etruscans.

pl830595307.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl830595307.description: Gallese is a settlement located about 14 km north of Civita Castellana. It was active especially in Faliscan times and again during late antiquity and the middle ages.

pl305624956.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl305624956.description: Trevinano is a human settlement in Italy, located in the Province of Viterbo of northern Lazio. In antiquity the site was settled by Etruscans. In the eleventh century, the powerful Boncompagni-Ludovisi family built a castle there.

pl770702013.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl770702013.description: A Medieval Christian sanctuary along the Via Appia, perhaps best known as the Church of Domine Quo Vadis.

pl933683601.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl933683601.description: On the hill of Grignano, located on the outskirts of Montebuono, the remains of a Roman villa were first excavated in the nineteenth century in the area of the church of "S. Pietro ad centum muros". Excavation in the 1990s revealed further villa remains beneath the church and in the vicinity of its cemetery. Epigraphic evidence attesting to the consulship of M. Vipsanius Agrippa was discovered immured in the church (CIL 9.4677 and 9.4779).

pl87797229.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl87797229.description: An eleventh and tenth century B.C. settlement in south Etruria.

pl765136701.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl765136701.description: Vejano, located in the Province of Viterbo, is located on the Mignone river approximately 60 km northwest of Rome. While the most visible monument on the site today is the fifteenth century castle known as "La Rocca", the site has a long settlement history reaching back to the Bronze Age.

pl483627782.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl483627782.description: A rural site located in the territory of Volterra.

pl403660414.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl403660414.description: A modern comune located in the territory of Rieti, Lazio. The Rieti Survey identified this as a likely Roman-period settlement covering more than 5 ha. Material evidence suggests occupation from ca. the sixth century B.C. until the sixth century A.D.

pl589093011.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl589093011.description: Poggibonsi is an ancient and medieval center in the province of Siena on the Elsa river. The city sits along the Via Francigena.

pl989027460.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl989027460.description: Monte Rovello was an important Etruscan settlement covering ca. 5 hectares with occupation stretching from the Bronze Age to the Hellenistic period.

pl344747000.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl344747000.description: Evidence of a Roman shipyard has been discovered at the locality of Stifone within the comune of Le Mole of the town of Narni. This shpiyard was connected to an artificial canal dug adjacent to the river Nera.

pl395149981.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl395149981.description: A Roman villa commonly associated with Q. Voconius Pollio that was excavated in the nineteenth century.

pl917618128.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl917618128.description: A Roman villa in the locality of Torelle at San Potito Sannitico.

pl597395300.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl597395300.description: Site of a large Roman villa, the remains of which were incorporated into the church of Santa Maria in Legarano. The early phases of the villa likely date to the early imperial period. At some point the villa became an Imperial property as it was donated to Pope Sylvester by Constantine.

pl678263113.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl678263113.description: A series of rock-cut dwellings and buildings.

pl24162247.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl24162247.description: Ninfa is now a garden landscape covering more than 100 hectares in the territory of Cisterna di Latina. In archaeological terms, this landscape includes many remains stretching from protohistory to the Middle Ages.

pl826462996.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl826462996.description: Moregine, immediately to the south of the archaeological site of Pompeii, is the findspot of an important archaeological assemblage buried by seismic activity that preceded the final eruption of Vesuvius in A.D. 79.

pl203215665.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl203215665.description: San Gimignano, which originated as an Etruscan settlement, is best known as a Medieval town renowned for its fortified towers.

pl703739111.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl703739111.description: Monte Amiata is a lava dome located about 20 km northwest of Lake Bolsena in Italy.

pl336470346.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl336470346.description: Capalbio is a municipality in the Province of Grosseto. It is first attested in A.D. 805 when Charlemagne donated the locality to the Abbey of the Tre Fontane.

pl885624151.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl885624151.description: A site of ancient thermal baths.

pl780853071.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl780853071.description: Roman ruins were discovered on the shores of Lake Balaton.

pl675229373.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl675229373.description: The archaeological site of Torre d'Ischia was identified in 1982, with evidence for Proto-Villanovan occupation.

pl857433537.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl857433537.description: An Umbro-Roman temple of Iuppiter on the slopes of Monte Catria.

pl702892067.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl702892067.description: A Roman villa of the third and fourth centuries A.D.

pl276094798.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl276094798.description: Muggia's beginnings as a prehistoric fortified village (castelliere) came ca. the eighth and seventh centuries B.C. This territory came under Roman control in the 170s BC. In 931, king Hugh of Italy donated Muggia to the Patriarch of Aquileia.

pl757679976.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl757679976.description: A settlement that was an important center of the Vestini in the Abruzzo.

pl232079422.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl232079422.description: The present town of Cetona grew around the rocca (fortress) of the tenth century A.D., although occupation at the site reaches back to the Paleolithic when a number of caves show evidence for human activity. There are also indications of an Etruscan phase of occupation.

pl531323023.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl531323023.description: Extensive areas of rock-cut tombs near Falerii Veteres (modern Civita Castellana, Italy).

pl52385299.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl52385299.description: An archaeological area along the Via Ostiensis with evidence of human activity stretching from the Archaic period to the time of the Roman Empire. SIgnificant archaeological features include an extensive necropolis and a Roman bathing facility.

pl18528486.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl18528486.description: A minor Catholic basilica in Rome, Santa Croce in Gerusalemme is also a titular church in rione Esquilino and one of the Seven Pilgrim Churches. The church was consecrated ca. 325 to house relics of the Passion of Jesus Christ brought to Rome from the Holy Land by Empress St. Helena.

q693884.dateNote: 1701 is when the present church was begun. A church here is first recorded in 1137, and legend says it is older still.

q2004104.dateNote: The church you see now was begun in 1723 by Carlo Francesco Dotti. The first church here was built in 1194.

q97352832.dateNote: The year shown only stands for the 18th century.

pl17452629.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl17452629.description: The site of a Neolithic village located in the territory of Matera in southern Italy. The site was initially discovered in the 1890s by Domenico Ridola.

q237742.died: 29 January 1844, Palace of the Infanta Carlota

q134114.summary: On 2 December 1805 near Austerlitz, in today's Czech Republic, Napoleon's Grande Armée defeated a combined Russian and Austrian army.

q273314.died: 18 October 1889, Staten Island, New York City

q348527.born: 19 June 1842, St. Peter in der Au

q78531.born: 24 October 1844, Main building of the TU Wien

q975807.dateNote: Died 10 January 1891 (29 December 1890 in the old calendar).

q1076439.dateNote: The church is far older than 1860: it goes back to the 300s and was rebuilt in 1217 and again in the 1700s. 1860 could not be confirmed.

cur-fossil-solnhofen.dateNote: In 1861 the quarries gave up a single feather, then a skeleton of Archaeopteryx — a dinosaur with wings. The limestone formed in a warm lagoon about 150 million years ago (Late Jurassic).

q588124.born: 30 May 1862, Dolenčice, near Škofja Loka, Carniola

q4120.dateNote: 1869 is when it got town rights. It grew up from about 1810, when the Danube became the border between Bavaria and Württemberg.

q78971.died: 1 June 1945, The Bronx, New York City

q31793.died: 2 December 1947, Civilian Internment Enclosure No. 22, Regensburg

cur-fossil-mladec.dateNote: In 1881 Josef Szombathy began digging these caves in Moravia, Czech Republic, and found skulls and bones of early modern humans. Dated directly, they are about 31,000 years old (0.031 million years).
cur-fossil-mladec.summary: Moravian caves with some of the oldest bones of modern humans in Europe.

cur-fossil-predmosti.dateNote: In 1894 Karel Jaroslav Maška found a grave of about 18 people, laid among mammoth bones, at Předmostí near Přerov in Moravia. They are about 26,000 years old (0.026 million years). Most of the bones were lost in a fire in 1945.
cur-fossil-predmosti.summary: A Moravian hill where Ice Age mammoth hunters buried their dead.

cur-fossil-krapina.dateNote: In 1899 Dragutin Gorjanović-Kramberger began digging Hušnjakovo hill at Krapina, Croatia. By 1905 he had found about 900 bones of Neanderthals, about 0.13 million years old.
cur-fossil-krapina.summary: One of the richest Neanderthal sites, with hundreds of bones.

pl881305239.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl881305239.description: The Civita Giuliana is located in the northern suburbium of Pompeii, about 700 meters from the city walls. Thus far the site has produced archaeological evidence of suburban villas in Pompeii's hinterland. Early twentieth-century excavations were carried out here, only to be published in 1994. Clandestine looting at the site brought about a cooperative effort to resume excavations in the interests of heritage protection in 2017.

pl446574720.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl446574720.description: The so-called "Ponte di Diocleziano" in the local comune of San Lazzaro di Fossombrone was a Roman bridge along the Via Flaminia in the valley of the Metaurus river. The Roman bridge was completely destroyed during the Second World War.

pl432766.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl442527.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl442527.description: Remains of a fourth-century B.C. sanctuary situated at a spring known as Caput aquae, from which the modern toponym is most likely derived.

pl442649.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl865293111.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl865293111.description: A bridge over the Metauro River built initially in the thirteenth century. The original bridge was destroyed in 1765 and rebuilt in 1782. The bridge was again destroyed in 1944 and was rebuilt in 1946.

pl669601729.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl669601729.description: A necropolis of the Terramare culture, located in the present-day province of Modena, Italy.

pl471408012.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl471408012.description: Documented in media released by the Croatian Ministry of Culture and Media in 2025, remains of a small theater or odeon of Roman date have been identified and consolidated under the early 20th-century city hall of modern Sisak in Croatia (ancient Segestica/Siscia). Existence of a theater at Sisak was previously mooted on the basis of a Latin inscription mentioning a "magister mimariorum" (leader of a mime-troop?) discovered in the 19th century in a "Weingarten" there, but it is unclear if there was an ancient relationship between this inscription, its original social context, and the newly discovered monument.

pl977694002.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl977694002.description: Tratturo Caniò is an archaeological site in the territory of the ancient city of Setia, on the Pontine Plain of Lazio, Italy. An archaic temple sacred to Iuno is known at the site, and archaeological prospection in 2009 revealed earlier Bronze Age and Iron Age remains.

pl147181485.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl147181485.description: The Paglicci cave or Grotta Paglicci is located near Rignano Garganico, Apulia, in southern Italy. Discovered in the 1950s, the cave is an important archaeological site documenting life in the Paleolithic period. In addition to artifact finds and zooarchaeological information, the cave provides evidence of the harvesting of wild oats ca. 36,000 BCE. The cave also includes Paleolithic mural art.

pl589881342.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl589881342.description: The so-called "Baths of the Swimmer" or "Terme del Nuotatore" (V,X,3) in region 5 of the ancient city of Ostia takes its modern name from a partially preserved black-and-white mosaic pavement. These baths were built in the late first century CE during the reign of Domitian. The complex was rebuilt during the Antonine period. The complex remained in use until ca. 250. The site was first excavated during 1938-1942. Andrea Carandini directed another campaign of excavation from 1966 to 1975.

pl445462065.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl445462065.description: An Etruscan farm site located in the Albegna valley.

q351683.born: 24 February 1903, Imperial Free City of Trieste

q84335.dateNote: When he died is not known; he is thought to have died in Damascus in 2001 or about 2010.

q432927.died: 18 June 1942, Saints Cyril and Methodius Cathedral

q989.born: 18 May 1920, Holy Father John Paul II Family Home, Wadowice

q2494.born: 16 April 1927, Birth house of Benedict XVI

q160717.died: 11 February 2008, Walter Reed National Military Medical Center

q503633.dateNote: 1934 is when the towns of Sulzbach and Rosenberg joined. Sulzbach castle goes back to the 700s, but no firm first-record year was found for the town.

q1054.placeNote: Pinned at the centre of Italy. Wikidata records the country where this happened but not a place within it, so the marker shows the country, not the spot.

q207406.dateNote: 1939 is when the towns of Moson and Magyaróvár merged. Both are much older (Moson is a medieval town).

q26776.died: 15 September 2020, University Clinical Center of the Republika Srpska

cur-fossil-kulna.dateNote: From 1961 to 1976 Karel Valoch dug this cave in the Moravian Karst, Czech Republic, and found Neanderthal bones, including part of an upper jaw. They are about 50,000 years old (0.05 million years).
cur-fossil-kulna.summary: A cave in the Moravian Karst where Neanderthal bones and tools were dug up.

cur-fossil-vertesszolos.dateNote: In 1965 László Vértes's team found the back of a human skull, nicknamed "Samu", among stone tools and burnt bones in a travertine quarry at Vértesszőlős, Hungary. It is about 0.3–0.5 million years old.
cur-fossil-vertesszolos.summary: A skull bone from Hungary of a human who lived several hundred thousand years ago.

q62069250.dateNote: A small Roman fort on the Raetian Limes, built in the 2nd century AD. 1973 is not when it was built.

cur-fossil-vindija.dateNote: From 1974 Mirko Malez dug Neanderthal bones out of this cave in northern Croatia. In 2010 DNA from three of them gave the first draft of the whole Neanderthal genome. The bones are more than 40,000 years old (0.04 million years).
cur-fossil-vindija.summary: A Croatian cave whose bones gave the first Neanderthal genome.

pl640651840.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl640651840.description: The Casale Ciuffa occupied the site of a Roman villa; this site now lies within the footprint of the Parco degli Ulivi in the modern comune of Colonna, Lazio.

pl906461649.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl906461649.description: Allerona is an Italian town in the province of Terni (Umbria). It is the findspot of a Trajanic milestone.

pl851457946.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl851457946.description: Remains of a Roman theater were identified in the 20th century in the vicinity of modern Piano La Roma in the municipal territory of Casoli, Italy. Its construction is estimated to date to the end of the first century BCE.

pl687957706.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl687957706.description: A Hellenistic fortified site (?oppidum) near Capranica (Viterbo).

pl104349764.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl104349764.description: The Tomba del Sileno is an Etruscan tomb at the Sovana Archaeological Park in the province of Grosseto. Dating from the third century BCE, the tomb derives its name from a bas-relief resembling the head of a Silen.

pl588365926.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl588365926.description: What would become Medieval Rota was once a pagus of Etruscan Caere. Writing in PECS, Mario Torelli describes this an an important Archaic center in the area of Tolfa.

pl652994900.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl652994900.description: The Italian comune of Belmonte Piceno is located in the province of Ascoli Piceno. The environs of this modern settlement have produced a range of archaeological evidence of Iron Age populations, including Latin inscriptions.

pl214908563.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl214908563.description: A Samnite sanctuary of ancient Capua that was initially discovered in 1845. Active from the sixth century B.C. until the first century B.C., the Santuario di Fondo Patturelli is noted for its architectural terracotta as well as for the presence of a sacred maternal cult.

pl697987396.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl697987396.description: The sanctuary of Monte Papalucio was an important Messapian sanctuary. It is located on the mountain of the same name in the territory of Oria in the province of Brindisi. The deities Demeter and Persephone were venerated in this cave sanctuary.

pl264713171.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl264713171.description: Örvényes, County of Veszprém, Hungary, was the site of a Roman settlement.

pl830595308.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl830595308.description: Grotta Porciosa, near Borghetto, was the site of a small but prosperous settlement in the Ager Faliscus.

pl199996184.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl199996184.description: A probable Roman villa site at Lio Piccolo in the Venice lagoon, with a well-preserved, first-century oyster tank made of brick and wood.

pl766163673.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl766163673.description: The underwater archaeological park of Baia is a protected marine and cultural heritage area. Submerged beneath the waters of the Gulf of Naples are various Roman-period archaeological remains, including those of harbors, villas, shrines, and nymphaea.

pl916776658.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl916776658.description: The estate (tenuta) of Pantano Borghese is one of the oldest land holdings in the Agro Romano and was acquired by the Colonna family in 1613. Much of this low-lying area was once marshland at the margins of the crater lakes of this part of Latium. Thomas Ashby's work on the Roman Campagna documented numerous archaeological and epigraphical remains in this zone, including extensive remains of Roman villas.

pl965286144.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl965286144.description: A villa rustica was excavated near Licenza in 1913, the exact position of which is no longer known. This site included a possible granary room, as well as a torcular.

pl986408803.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl986408803.description: A terraced sanctuary of the Samnite culture that was in use from the archaic period to the third century B.C.

pl744307622.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl744307622.description: Pianello di Genga, located in Italy's Ancona province, was the site of a Final Bronze Age settlement, as attested by an extensive necropolis.

pl565807319.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl565807319.description: A series of decorated early Christian tombs dating to the fourth century CE is located in the town of Sopianae, in the Roman Province of Pannonia. The Early Christian Necropolis of Pécs was enrolled as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2000.

pl249663476.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl249663476.description: Pontecorvo is a comune located in the province of Frosinone, Lazio, Italy.

pl465281214.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl465281214.description: The Necropolis della Casetta at Blera contains numerous dado-type tombs.

pl133309568.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl133309568.description: An imperial necropolis with at least 326 tombs was identified at modern Castel Malnome (Ponte Galeria) in Italy. Archaeological evidence marks these as burials belonging to working-class people of the Roman imperial period, with most graves having either no grave goods or very few. The osteoarchaeological analysis led excavators to speculate that the individuals buried here many have worked in the salt flats.

pl597689488.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl597689488.description: Montefalco is a hilltop town in Italy's present-day Umbria region. Its ancient toponymy and settlement history remain debated, although it is the findspot of several municipal inscriptions in Latin.

pl122145682.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl122145682.description: An ancient necropolis located in the modern Parco della Serenissima that was initially discovered via construction works in 1997. The necropolis is located, in ancient terms, in a landscape between the line of the via Collatina and that of the via Praenestina. The excavations also revealed traces of first-millennium BCE agricultural activity.

pl149580279.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl149580279.description: A pre-Roman center located in the territory of Allifae.

pl430660565.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl430660565.description: The "La Petrina" necropolis is associated with ancient Narce and was in use from the eighth to the third centuries BCE.

pl643083925.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl643083925.description: An Etruscan necropolis at Tarquinia with more than 175 tombs.

pl214502051.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl214502051.description: A Roman "villa rustica" occupied from ca. 80 - 240 CE, located in the Innviertel region, northeast of the Austrian town of Altheim, village of Weirading (Kiriberg district). This is one of three such sites in the general vicinity of Altheim.

pl131901105.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl131901105.description: A necropolis located to the north of ancient Falerii Veteres containing more than 67 tombs.

pl454350148.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl454350148.description: A Late Neolithic to Chalcolithic settlement in the vicinity of the Medieval Torre Spaccata in Rome. The earlier settlement remains were truncated by activity in the Roman period that included road pavement.

pl971724591.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl971724591.description: The modern Italian comune of Tolfa is 24 kilometers northeast of Cerveteri. Its environs contain several ancient sites, dating from prehistory as well as the time of the Roman Empire.

pl931492631.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl931492631.description: An amphora production site with kiln was identified in the 1990s at a place called Felceto, approximately 10km south of ancient Tifernum Tiberinum (modern Città di Castello) and 2km east of the Tiber on a tributary (i.e., somewhere to the east of modern Cinquemiglia and Promano). The site has not been excavated.

pl960808205.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl960808205.description: In the introductory essay for Map 41 of the Barrington Atlas published in the Map-by-Map Directory, Vico Pancellorum is mentioned as a toponym with likely ancient origins, but absent is any specific evidence to that effect. Vico Pancellorum is a small Tuscan village located in the Province of Lucca. It is situated at 630 meters above sea level at the foot of Balzo Nero.

pl960808207.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl960808207.description: Vicopisano is located in the Province of Pisa, some 50 km west of Florence and 15 km east of Pisa. In the Middle Ages, Vicopisano was a fortified center of the Republic of Pisa that was conquered by Florence in 1406. W.V. Harris asserts in the introductory essay for Map 41 of the Barrington Atlas that it is possible that the toponym "Vicopisano" has roots in the ancient Roman world.

pl348038268.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl348038268.description: An imperial villa located at Tor Vergata in the suburbium of Rome.

pl363892614.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl363892614.description: Trestina, located in the Val di Chiana of Umbria, was the site of the accidental discovery in 1878 of important Orientalizing-period bronzes.

pl220822469.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl220822469.description: The bridge known as the Ponte del Viceré de Ribera crosses the Fosso di Sant'Andrea on the line of the Via Appia. The viceroy of Naples, one Parefàn de Ribera, renovated the bridge in 1568. During the Second World War, the bridge was bombed and was eventually restored in 2005.

cur-fossil-iharkut.dateNote: In 2000 Attila Ősi found dinosaur bones in an old bauxite mine at Iharkút in the Bakony Hills, Hungary. Finds since include the armoured dinosaur Hungarosaurus. The rock is about 85 million years old (Late Cretaceous). Wikidata pins the formation at a rounded point by Iharkút.
cur-fossil-iharkut.summary: An old mine in Hungary where many Late Cretaceous dinosaurs have been dug up.
